navier_fit: All hops sit well under Pioneer II's 70 nm all-electric range over calm, protected reef waters — the cleanest possible product-market fit. Luxury resorts (Song Saa, Koh Russey, Lila) compete on guest experience, where a quiet, stable, zero-wake foiling arrival is a tangible upgrade over diesel speedboats. The signed WorldBridge/Lila partnership gives Navier an on-the-ground anchor, local-sales channel and reference site to expand across the archipelago.

summary: Cambodia's southern coast around Sihanoukville is the country's island-hopping engine: the mainland gateway port and airport feed a ring of resort islands — Koh Rong and Koh Rong Sanloem (Saracen Bay), the private islands of Song Saa and Koh Russey (Bamboo Island), Koh Ta Kiev, and the Ream National Park / Lila private-island cluster. Every transfer is a short, protected hop (Sihanoukville to the islands runs ~10-40 minutes by boat; all legs sit comfortably under 30 nm), making this a textbook Pioneer II all-electric market. Demand is overwhelmingly luxury-tourism led and accelerating: ~63% of Cambodia's hotel pipeline is in the luxury segment and island tourism is roughly doubling year-over-year. Today's transfers run on diesel speedboats with inconsistent comfort and wake; a foiling-electric layer offers fast, stable, quiet, zero-wake transit ideal for protected reef waters and the high-end guest experience these resorts are built around. Navier's May 2026 partnership with the WorldBridge Group — one of Cambodia's largest conglomerates and developer of Lila Resort on a pristine private island — anchors the market with first-vessel delivery in 2026 and a multi-vessel, local-sales collaboration to follow.
tagline: Cambodia's island-hopping coast — luxury resorts blooming across Koh Rong, Koh Russey and the Ream private-island cluster, all reached today by aging diesel speedboats over short, calm hops.
